Quick triage notes (initial):
- Scope: spike is concentrated on the hosted API pool serving long-context variants (32k). Nearby pools with smaller context targets unchanged.
- Metrics (last 3 hours, sampled): GPU util 92-98% under these payloads, % of requests with >24k tokens increased dramatically; average batch packing size decreased (packing inefficiency). Host-level swap activity observed on 2 of 6 hosts serving the tenant; memory high-water marks reached with sporadic OOM avoidance paths (driver-side).
- Hypothesis: long-context requests are thrashing KV cache and causing inefficient kernel selection + host memory pressure leading to per-request stalls and backend retries at the infra layer — measurable as p99 tail.

Immediate mitigations we can attempt (ordered by speed):
1) Canary route CareBridge to a higher-priority pool with warmed quantization kernels and slightly higher concurrency; this requires capacity but minimal code change (~30-45m ops).
2) Enforce a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for 32k requests (config flag) to reduce contention.
3) Deploy a model-variant fallback rule: if request length >24k, route to a 16k-optimized variant that preserves prefix and only truncates lower-priority tail context. This needs runtime rule deployment (~2-3 hours).
4) Short-term: enable "graceful truncation" in the edge that preserves system context and drops trailing tokens when length exceeds 28k — simple config flip (~45m).

Longer-term (post-mortem): KV eviction strategy improvements, smarter batch packing for long sequences, and a host-level memory-pressure autoscaling trigger.

I attached a perf snapshot (perf-snapshot-20281011.png) and the sample payload. I’ll start a mitigation-runbook and begin the canary route.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20281011.png, carebridge-sample-32k-requests.json

Laura Bennett
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
